handoffs/LESSONS_FROM_COLDERWATER_2026-10-08.md (lesson 2: one documented weight scheme, no weight steering; customer audit compares failed vs passed average weight and recomputes with equal weights)
evidence: DIMENSION WEIGHTS: task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the frozen template (sha256 95f70d6e06aae5e765b2309d88c444aa36d4cd82763ea2212781b6a99311bbba both): [weights] functional = 0.6, polish = 0.2, visual = 0.2; [gates] render = 0.0, constraints = 0.0; [floors] functional = 0.05. tools/score.py (identical to template, diff empty) computes weighted = sum(w*score)/sum(w) and zeroes reward unless gates and the functional floor pass. Functionality therefore carries 60% and structure/style (visual) only 20%. MAX NON-FUNCTIONAL CONTRIBUTION: polish+visual cap at 0.4; but every polish criterion (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume) requires working live updates, conversations, sends or sign-in, so a stub earns ~0 polish. A pretty but nearly dead app must clear functional > 0.05 (>3.05 of 61 functional weight units, i.e. at least four real behaviours such as job_open+add_candidate+add_email_rules+arrive_bottom) and then reaches at most about 0.6*0.066 + 0.2 visual ~= 0.24; it cannot farm style. PER-CRITERION SCHEME: every scored judge.toml carries the single documented comment '# Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief (Visual Likert rows are equal).' (functional/judge.toml:23, polish:17, visual:17). Measured with tomllib: functional 44 criteria, sum 61.0, {1:21, 1.5:12, 2:11}; polish 5, sum 9.5, {2:4, 1.5:1}; visual 5 likert, all weight 1. Every 2.0 functional row maps to an explicit brief sentence in instruction.md: hro_stale_refused ('the refusal should say who'), hro_bulk_all_or_none ('all of them or none'), hro_undo_restores/hro_undo_conflict ('undo my last move... as long as nobody has touched those cards'), hro_refused_put_back ('put the card back where it really is and tell me why'), hro_live_board ('within fifteen seconds without a reload'), hro_thread_earlier ('pull in earlier ones'), hro_unread_counts ('Unread counts need to be right for each person'), hro_unread_scrolled_up ('leave my place alone and just tell me there is something new'), hro_drafts ('A reply I have not sent stays with that conversation...'), hro_candidate_private ('They must never see our internal notes...'). The brief's own framing ('the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts') justifies concurrency/preservation as the 2.0 tier. 1.5 rows are brief-named features (move_one_stage, reorder, interview_full, bulk_move, bulk_places, msg_exchange, thread_latest, seen, candidate_view, restart, anonymous, thread_access); 1.0 rows are rules-file details (job_open, add_candidate, email rules, reject/reopen details, manager/observer/candidate authorization, refusal_status, undo_once, activity, notes, msg_compose, candidate_linked). No functional criterion grades structure or style; none is weighted by difficulty against the brief. Foundational rows at 1.0/1.5 (open job, add candidate, one-stage move, message exchange) are prerequisites for many other rows, so their effective weight is much larger than their nominal weight; this is not under-weighting. NO STEERING: read-only git show of HEAD/HEAD~1/HEAD~2 functional judge.toml shows the prior candidate used 145-152 criteria with fractional weights (0.12056737, 0.4822695, ...); the frozen candidate replaced that with the clean 1/1.5/2 scheme, consistent with Colderwater lesson 2. Gate criteria carry weight = 1 under all_pass and zero reward mass (row 43 territory). EQUAL-WEIGHT SENSITIVITY (lesson 2 customer audit, computed from the scheme, not from runs): worst-case divergence between weighted and equal-weight functional means is +/-0.111 (pass only 1.0/1.5 rows: 39/61=0.639 vs 33/44=0.750; pass only 2.0 rows: 22/61=0.361 vs 11/44=0.250), i.e. at most +/-0.067 reward. Because the 2.0 tier is the concurrency edge cases a target model is most likely to fail, a model's failed rows will probably have a higher average weight than its passed rows; that is the pattern the customer audit inspects. It is defensible here by the brief text above, but it is unmeasured. Plausible-broken-app probe: an app with no server-side authorization at all loses observer_readonly, candidate_no_staff, mgr_early_refused, mgr_other_job, notes (other-manager leg), refusal_status (1.0 each), thread_access and anonymous (1.5 each), ~9/61 = 0.148 functional = ~0.089 reward, plus candidate_private (2.0) if anything leaks; the penalty is spread but material, not hidden. Conforming-alternative probe: weights cannot make a conforming app fail; a conforming app scores 1.0 regardless of weights. RISK: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' So the customer-audit comparison (average weight of failed vs passed criteria, equal-weight recompute) and real reward-ordering evidence for this weighting are not measured. Required missing evidence remains a risk; it is not waived.
